books.title: The Story of Civilization I–IV
books.author: Will Durant
books.blurb: Our Oriental Heritage, The Life of Greece, Caesar and Christ and The Age of Faith — four volumes in one illustrated pass.

related.why: The Durants' own distillation of these volumes into thirteen chapters.
The primary source sitting under Caesar and Christ.
The same sweep, argued from geography rather than character.

books.pdf: Durant — The Story of Civilization I–IV.pdf

books.title: The History of Rome
books.author: Livy
books.blurb: Ab Urbe Condita — the early history, Rome and Italy, the war with Hannibal, and Rome in the Mediterranean.

related.why: Durant's Caesar and Christ retells this material as narrative history.
The same empire three centuries on, seen from inside the emperor's head.
What the Durants think recurs in exactly this kind of record.

books.title: The Lessons of History
books.author: Will & Ariel Durant
books.blurb: Thirteen short chapters distilling four decades of writing history into what actually recurs.

related.why: The eleven volumes this book distils.
Michael Saylor, whose forecast this is, recommends the Durants' book.
The Durants' chapter on war, argued at full length.

books.title: Guns, Germs, and Steel
books.author: Jared Diamond
books.blurb: Yali's question, and the twenty-five year answer: why geography and not biology set the shape of the modern world.

related.why: The institutional rebuttal to geography.
Deutsch's objection: explanations, not environments, drive history.
The horse and gunpowder conquests, told as military history.

books.title: The Causes of Portuguese Backwardness
books.author: Nuno Palma
books.blurb: Why Portugal is rich by world standards and poor by European ones — a quantitative history that dates the fall precisely.

related.why: The geographic explanation this book's chronology is written against.
Recurrence as a way of reading history, next to Palma's insistence on dates.
Both books are mostly about not mistaking a story for a cause.
The same mechanism — a windfall that lets a crown stop asking — argued across the world.

books.title: Why Nations Fail
books.author: Daron Acemoglu & James A. Robinson
books.blurb: Institutions, not geography or culture — the inclusive/extractive argument, the cases it stands on, and an audit of how its predictions have aged.

related.why: The geographic answer this book was written to demolish — and whose author then reviewed it.
The same mechanism run over four centuries of one country, with much better data.
The monopoly the virtuous-circle chapter uses to prove an inclusive system can break its own most powerful man.

books.title: A History of Warfare
books.author: John Keegan
books.blurb: War as culture rather than policy: stone, flesh, iron and fire, and the limits of weather, walls, armies and supply.

related.why: Why some societies conquered others, argued from geography instead of culture.
The Roman way of war, as Rome's own historian told it.
The Durants on war as one of history's constants.

books.title: The Beginning of Infinity
books.author: David Deutsch
books.blurb: Progress comes from creating good explanations and exposing them to criticism. There is no final theory — only better ones.

related.why: The epistemology this book is built on.
The geographic explanation of history Deutsch argues against.
Fallibilism from the trader's side: what outcomes can't teach you.

books.title: Objective Knowledge
books.author: Karl Popper
books.blurb: An evolutionary approach: the solution to induction, the three worlds, and the source of Deutsch's epistemology.

related.why: Deutsch's extension of this book, forty years later.
Induction as a practical hazard rather than a philosophical one.
A long historical argument worth testing against Popper's standard for explanations.

books.title: Meditations
books.author: Marcus Aurelius
books.blurb: Twelve books of notes a Roman emperor wrote to himself, mostly on campaign, arguing with his own worst impulses.

related.why: The Rome he inherited, written by the historian his tutors gave him.
Taleb's Stoicism is drawn from exactly this, applied to markets.
The same discipline restated for a modern reader, minus the empire.

books.title: The Ethics of Liberty
books.author: Murray N. Rothbard
books.blurb: Self-ownership, homesteading and the rule against aggression, built into a legal code and turned on the State.

related.why: The value-free economics this book supplies the ethics for.
States as extraction, argued by historians rather than from first principles.
The Stoics, where the idea of a natural law began.

books.title: Fooled by Randomness
books.author: Nassim Nicholas Taleb
books.blurb: The hidden role of chance in life and in markets — and why a good outcome does not prove a good decision.

related.why: The problem of induction, which Taleb treats as a survival problem.
The Stoic source Taleb keeps returning to.
One long career to test the book's argument about skill and luck against.

books.title: Titan
books.author: Ron Chernow
books.blurb: The man who organised American oil, was broken up for it by the Supreme Court, then gave away more than anyone alive ever had.

related.why: The same question of method and scale, a century apart.
How much of a record like this is skill, and how you would ever know.
Leverage and compounding, stated as principle rather than biography.

books.title: The Almanack of Naval Ravikant
books.author: Eric Jorgenson
books.blurb: Specific knowledge, accountability and leverage; judgment, mental models, and what wealth is actually for.

related.why: The same compiler, the same method, a very different subject.
The Stoic spine underneath most of the happiness half.
A useful check on advice assembled from one person's outcomes.

books.title: The Book of Elon
books.author: Eric Jorgenson
books.blurb: Musk's method compiled from his own words: first-principles costing, The Algorithm, and what a curated record can carry.

related.why: Jorgenson's earlier book, and the template this one follows.
The nineteenth-century version of building at this scale.
Another technologist's forecast, now old enough to be scored.

books.title: The Mobile Wave
books.author: Michael J. Saylor
books.blurb: A forecast from 2012, most striking where it has since become invisible infrastructure — and most useful in its blind spots.

related.why: A newer forecast from inside the industry, not yet scoreable.
Why long-range prediction fails, stated as epistemology.
What actually happens when a new infrastructure gets organised.

books.title: Man, Economy, and State
books.author: Murray N. Rothbard
books.blurb: Economics deduced from one axiom, “man acts”: interest, capital, money and the business cycle, then the same logic turned on the state.

related.why: Producing versus taking, argued from history rather than deduced from an axiom.
The monopoly Rothbard's Chapter 10 says a free market cannot hold, told as a life.
The opposite method: conjecture and refutation instead of deduction from first principles.
